questionText: Prove that $\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = \tan\theta$ for all $\theta$ such that $\sin 2\theta \neq 0$.
markingScheme:
State the double-angle identity $1 - \cos 2\theta = 2\sin^2\theta$ **(1 mark)**
State the double-angle identity $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ **(1 mark)**
Substitute both into the left-hand side **(1 mark)**
Simplify to obtain $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ **(1 mark)**
Conclude equals $\tan\theta$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.explanation: Divide numerator and denominator by $2\sin\theta$ (valid since $\sin 2\theta \neq 0$ implies $\sin\theta \neq 0$): $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
